questions.prompt: What is BACnet primarily designed to provide?
options: Vendor-independent communication for building automation and control systems
A proprietary controller programming language that requires every participating product to use the same vendor runtime and source-code format
A protocol intended to replace electrical codes, controller safety requirements, and every manufacturer installation standard
A cloud-only building database that stores telemetry but defines no interoperable device, object, service, or network behavior
questions.explanation: BACnet standardizes how building automation devices represent information and exchange control, status, alarm, schedule, and other data across vendors.

questions.prompt: How does BACnet model a device's application data?
options: As numbered PLC registers only
As a collection of objects with properties
As rows in a required SQL database
As unstructured text messages
questions.explanation: BACnet uses an object-oriented model. Objects such as Analog Input and Schedule expose standardized properties.

questions.prompt: What two parts make up a BACnet Object Identifier?
options: Vendor ID and UDP port
Network number and MAC address
Object type and object instance
Device instance and IP address
questions.explanation: An Object Identifier combines an object type with an instance number that is unique for that type within the device.

questions.prompt: What is special about the Device object's instance number on a BACnet internetwork?
options: It must exactly match the final IPv4 octet of every interface, including interfaces that are not used for BACnet/IP communication
It is always zero because the BACnet network number, rather than the Device object, uniquely identifies each controller
It may be duplicated when devices are on different subnets
It should be unique across the BACnet internetwork
questions.explanation: Device instances are used for logical device identification and dynamic binding, so duplicates create ambiguous discovery and communication.

questions.prompt: Which BACnet service is required to be supported by every BACnet device?
options: ReadProperty
SubscribeCOV
ReinitializeDevice
WriteProperty
questions.explanation: ReadProperty is the baseline service required by all BACnet devices; other services depend on a device's claimed capabilities.

questions.prompt: Which service pair is used for BACnet device discovery?
options: SubscribeCOV and COVNotification
Who-Is and I-Am
Who-Has and I-Have
ReadProperty and WriteProperty
questions.explanation: A client sends Who-Is, optionally with a device-instance range, and matching devices answer with I-Am.

questions.prompt: What distinguishes a confirmed BACnet service from an unconfirmed service?
options: Confirmed services are restricted to encrypted MS/TP sessions and therefore cannot return acknowledgements or protocol errors
Confirmed services are always global broadcasts that every device must process even when the request names one specific destination
Confirmed services require an acknowledgement or error response
Confirmed services are always encrypted with TLS, while unconfirmed services are required to remain unencrypted on every data link
questions.explanation: Confirmed requests expect a response such as SimpleACK, ComplexACK, Error, Reject, or Abort. Unconfirmed requests do not.

questions.prompt: What does an APDU carry in BACnet?
options: Only Ethernet framing
Only an IPv4 header
The RS-485 electrical waveform
Application-layer service information
questions.explanation: The Application Protocol Data Unit encodes BACnet application services and their parameters.

questions.prompt: What is the main role of the BACnet NPDU?
options: Carry network-layer addressing and routing information
Store time-series trend samples and permanently archive every historical value reported by every object in the device
Define, issue, renew, and revoke the complete set of TLS certificates used by every BACnet/SC node and hub on the internetwork
Represent an analog process value together with its engineering units, reliability, event state, and command-priority array
questions.explanation: The Network Protocol Data Unit carries network-layer control and routing information around the application payload.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes BACnet's relationship to lower-layer networks?
options: BACnet operates only over Ethernet cabling and requires all compliant controllers to use the same Ethernet physical interface
BACnet defines application and networking behavior across multiple data-link technologies
BACnet requires every compliant device to implement BACnet/IP, BACnet/SC, MS/TP, ARC156, Ethernet, and all future data links simultaneously
BACnet is only an IP routing protocol
questions.explanation: BACnet keeps a consistent object, service, and network-layer model across supported data links, including BACnet/IP, BACnet/SC, MS/TP, and ARC156. ARC156 is the common BAS name for BACnet ARCNET at 156 kbps, typically carried on an EIA-485 physical layer.

questions.prompt: Which property normally contains the current value of an Analog Input object?
options: Event_State
Object_Name
Present_Value
Description
questions.explanation: Present_Value carries the object's current process value; Units explains the engineering units.

questions.prompt: Which property tells a client whether an analog value is degrees Celsius, percent, pascals, or another engineering unit?
options: Priority_Array
Reliability
Object_Type
Units
questions.explanation: The Units property supplies the standardized engineering-unit enumeration for applicable objects.

questions.prompt: Which four conditions are represented by the standard Status_Flags bit string?
options: In alarm, fault, overridden, out of service
Read, write, execute, delete
Online, offline, local, remote
High, low, open, closed
questions.explanation: Status_Flags reports IN_ALARM, FAULT, OVERRIDDEN, and OUT_OF_SERVICE in a consistent four-bit form.

questions.prompt: Why might a technician set an object's Out_Of_Service property to TRUE?
options: To enable BBMD forwarding and distribute BACnet/IP broadcasts to every remote subnet without configuring a distribution table
To permit testing a simulated value without relying on the physical input
To erase the object, its references, its historical records, and every command priority permanently from the controller database
To change its Device instance
questions.explanation: For objects that support it, Out_Of_Service decouples the represented value from the physical process so behavior can be tested.

questions.prompt: How many command priority levels are in the standard BACnet Priority_Array?
questions.explanation: Commandable objects use sixteen priorities, where priority 1 is highest and priority 16 is lowest.

questions.prompt: How does a BACnet client relinquish a command it previously wrote at a priority?
options: Write zero at priority 1
Delete the object
Send Who-Is
Write NULL at that same priority
questions.explanation: Writing NULL releases that slot. The effective value then comes from the next active priority or Relinquish_Default.

questions.prompt: What are the two standard states of a Binary Value's Present_Value?
options: Inactive and active
Normal and fault, as determined by Reliability
Open and closed only
Zero and one, with no configurable state text
questions.explanation: BACnet names binary present values INACTIVE and ACTIVE; display text may be customized using inactive and active text properties.

questions.prompt: How are states numbered for a Multi-state Value object?
options: Using only text with no number
Starting at 1
Starting at 0
Using negative integers
questions.explanation: BACnet multi-state Present_Value values are one-based, from 1 through Number_Of_States.

questions.prompt: Which BACnet object is intended to represent recurring weekly operation with date-specific exceptions?
options: File, using a separate record for every weekly transition
Loop, using its control action to encode calendar exceptions
Schedule
Accumulator
questions.explanation: Schedule objects combine a Weekly_Schedule with Exception_Schedule entries and write scheduled values to referenced properties.

questions.prompt: Which object is primarily used to store a time-ordered history of values or events?
options: Notification Class
Device, because Object_List stores a timestamped copy of every value
Command, because each action entry automatically becomes a historical record
Trend Log
questions.explanation: Trend Log and Trend Log Multiple objects maintain timestamped records for later retrieval.

questions.prompt: Why would a client use ReadPropertyMultiple instead of many individual ReadProperty requests?
options: To read several properties more efficiently in fewer transactions
To encrypt every property response and prevent other authenticated BACnet clients from reading the returned application data
To discover every IP router, BBMD peer, foreign device, and reachable BACnet network in a single confirmed application transaction
To change command priorities
questions.explanation: ReadPropertyMultiple can request multiple properties and objects in one confirmed transaction, reducing protocol overhead when supported.

questions.prompt: Which service changes the value of a writable BACnet property?
options: I-Am
WriteProperty
Who-Has
ReadRange
questions.explanation: WriteProperty sends a value, and optionally an array index and command priority, to a writable property.

questions.prompt: What is the main benefit of Change of Value reporting?
options: It replaces Who-Is, I-Am, Who-Has, I-Have, router discovery, address binding, and all other BACnet discovery mechanisms
It assigns BACnet network numbers, Device instances, and local MAC addresses automatically whenever a controller starts
Clients receive updates when a relevant value changes instead of polling continuously
All values are broadcast every second
questions.explanation: COV reduces needless polling by notifying subscribed clients when defined value or status changes occur.

questions.prompt: What must a recipient do after receiving a ConfirmedCOVNotification?
options: Send a Who-Is broadcast
Change its Device instance
Register as a foreign device
Return an acknowledgement or applicable error
questions.explanation: Confirmed notifications are confirmed services and therefore require a protocol response.

questions.prompt: Which service pair discovers an object by identifier or name?
options: Who-Has and I-Have
Who-Is and I-Am
TimeSynchronization and UTCTimeSynchronization
CreateObject and DeleteObject
questions.explanation: Who-Has asks which device contains an object; a device can answer with I-Have.

questions.prompt: What is a key protocol difference between TimeSynchronization and UTCTimeSynchronization?
options: There is no difference
One conveys local date/time and the other conveys UTC date/time
One is only for MS/TP and the other only for IP
One changes object priorities
questions.explanation: TimeSynchronization carries local time, while UTCTimeSynchronization carries Coordinated Universal Time for devices that support it.

questions.prompt: Why should access to ReinitializeDevice be tightly controlled?
options: It is required for normal discovery
It merely refreshes a browser page
It can restart or otherwise reinitialize a controller
It only reads public values
questions.explanation: ReinitializeDevice can disrupt controller operation and may support password parameters, so it should be protected operationally and by network policy.

questions.prompt: Which service is designed to transfer a portion of a BACnet File object's contents?
options: ReadRange
GetEnrollmentSummary
LifeSafetyOperation
AtomicReadFile
questions.explanation: AtomicReadFile and AtomicWriteFile transfer file data using stream or record access methods.

questions.prompt: Which service communicates an alarm or event transition to a recipient?
options: EventNotification
DeviceCommunicationControl
I-Am-Router-To-Network
WriteGroup
questions.explanation: ConfirmedEventNotification or UnconfirmedEventNotification conveys event state, timestamps, priority, and related event data.

questions.prompt: What problem does BACnet APDU segmentation solve?
options: Encrypting Device objects, object identifiers, property values, routing fields, and data-link headers independently inside each APDU
Transferring an application message larger than the parties' supported APDU size in multiple segments
Assigning and negotiating unique MS/TP MAC addresses across multiple EIA-485 trunks without any installer configuration
Forwarding IP broadcasts
questions.explanation: Segmentation divides a large confirmed transaction into sequenced APDU segments when both peers support the needed segmentation behavior.

questions.prompt: BACnet/IPv4 normally carries BVLL messages using which transport protocol?
options: SCTP
TCP
UDP
ICMP
questions.explanation: BACnet/IPv4 uses UDP, with BVLL providing BACnet-specific virtual-link functions such as broadcast management.

questions.prompt: What is the default BACnet/IP UDP port in decimal and hexadecimal?
questions.explanation: The default BACnet/IP port is 47808 decimal, conventionally written 0xBAC0.

questions.prompt: Why does a local BACnet/IP broadcast normally fail to reach devices on another IP subnet?
options: IP routers normally do not forward local subnet broadcasts
BACnet permits only one IPv4 subnet in an internetwork, so a second subnet is rejected even when BACnet routers are present
UDP cannot carry subnet-directed, local, or global broadcasts and therefore requires a separate TCP connection for every BACnet recipient
Every remote device must use TCP
questions.explanation: IP broadcast domains stop at routers, so BACnet needs broadcast management or another suitable architecture across subnets.

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of a BACnet Broadcast Management Device?
options: Terminate MS/TP wiring
Forward BACnet/IP broadcast traffic between configured IP subnets
Translate every BACnet object into Modbus registers
Assign Device instance numbers
questions.explanation: A BBMD distributes BACnet/IP broadcasts between IP broadcast domains according to its broadcast distribution configuration.

questions.prompt: What information is maintained in a BBMD's Broadcast Distribution Table?
options: Detailed MS/TP token statistics, baud rates, Max_Master values, and termination measurements for every connected serial trunk
TLS private keys, full certificate chains, revocation lists, trusted root authorities, and BACnet/SC node authorization policies
Other broadcast distribution peers and their addressing information
All object Present_Values
questions.explanation: The BDT identifies where a BBMD should forward distributed broadcasts; entries include peer addressing and mask information as applicable.

questions.prompt: What is stored in a BBMD's Foreign Device Table?
options: A permanent inventory of every Device object, including its object list, firmware revision, and complete network address binding
Only the network numbers advertised by BACnet routers, including hop counts, next-hop addresses, path costs, and route expiration times
Alarm acknowledgement history
Temporary foreign-device registrations with address and remaining lifetime
questions.explanation: The FDT records registered foreign devices and their time-to-live state so they can receive forwarded broadcasts.

questions.prompt: What should a foreign device do before its BBMD registration time-to-live expires?
options: Renew its registration
Change its UDP port
Send a global Who-Is continuously
Delete its Device object
questions.explanation: Foreign-device registration is leased. The foreign device must register again before expiry to continue receiving distributed broadcasts.

questions.prompt: Where does the BACnet Virtual Link Layer sit relative to the BACnet NPDU on BACnet/IP?
options: It is above the APDU
It encapsulates the NPDU for the IP data link
It is inside every object property
It replaces the application layer
questions.explanation: BVLL is the BACnet/IP virtual-link framing and function layer that carries NPDUs across the IP data link.

questions.prompt: Can multiple IP subnets participate in one BACnet network number?
options: Only when every participating controller is configured with the same IPv4 address, subnet mask, UDP port, and default gateway
Only over MS/TP
Yes, a BACnet/IP network can span IP subnets when broadcast management and addressing are designed correctly
No; each IPv4 host must have a different BACnet network number, even when all hosts share one local IP subnet and broadcast domain
questions.explanation: BACnet/IP can treat multiple IP subnets as one BACnet network; BBMDs or other specified mechanisms manage broadcasts across those subnets.

questions.prompt: What should a BBMD do with an incoming distributed broadcast intended for its local BACnet/IP network?
options: Convert the broadcast into individual confirmed WriteProperty requests addressed to every Device instance found in its binding table
Assign the message a new Device instance, source network, destination network, command priority, and transaction identifier
Drop all broadcasts unconditionally
Distribute it on the local BACnet/IP network according to BVLL rules
questions.explanation: The BBMD bridges the broadcast distribution mechanism to its local IP broadcast domain while applying BVLL forwarding rules.

questions.prompt: What does a BACnet network number identify?
options: A BACnet network segment in the internetwork
A single object property together with its datatype, command priority, event state, and most recently reported application value
A vendor organization together with its assigned identifier, product catalog, supported profiles, and proprietary object ranges
An alarm priority that determines recipient order, acknowledgement requirements, transition handling, and notification delivery
questions.explanation: Network numbers identify BACnet networks for network-layer routing; they do not identify individual devices.

questions.prompt: Which identifier is intended to remain meaningful across routed BACnet networks?
options: IPv4 subnet mask alone
Device instance number
Local MS/TP MAC address alone
Ethernet switch port number
questions.explanation: A Device instance identifies the BACnet device logically across the internetwork; a MAC address is meaningful on its local data link.

questions.prompt: What is the role of a BACnet router?
options: Store all trend history from every controller and provide permanent centralized retention for alarms, schedules, and audit records
Issue BTL certificates after testing each connected product for protocol conformance, interoperability, and site-specific sequence operation
Forward NPDUs between distinct BACnet networks
Forward Ethernet frames between switch ports only
questions.explanation: A BACnet router connects ports belonging to different BACnet network numbers and forwards network-layer traffic.

questions.prompt: Why are duplicate BACnet network numbers a serious design error?
options: Duplicate network numbers force every object property on both networks to read zero until each controller receives a new Device instance
They change all BACnet/IP traffic from UDP to TCP and force every MS/TP or ARC156 router to negotiate a TLS session
They disable TLS certificates
Routers cannot unambiguously determine the destination network path
questions.explanation: Network numbers must be unique within the BACnet internetwork so routing announcements and destinations are unambiguous.

questions.prompt: Which network-layer message asks routers whether they can reach a specified BACnet network?
options: Who-Is-Router-To-Network
Who-Is
Who-Has
Register-Foreign-Device
questions.explanation: Who-Is-Router-To-Network discovers a route; routers answer with I-Am-Router-To-Network when appropriate.

questions.prompt: What does I-Am-Router-To-Network communicate?
options: An alarm acknowledgement
A router's reachable BACnet network numbers
A device's object list
A BBMD's foreign-device lease
questions.explanation: Routers use I-Am-Router-To-Network to advertise the destination networks they can reach.

questions.prompt: Which BACnet destination network value represents a global broadcast?
questions.explanation: DNET 65535 is the BACnet global-broadcast destination. Its scope should be used deliberately because routers propagate it.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the Hop Count field in a routed BACnet NPDU?
options: Count the application objects traversed by a request so the destination can reject messages that reference too many object instances
Set and dynamically negotiate the MS/TP baud rate, Max_Master, Max_Info_Frames, station address, and token timeout on every traversed segment
Select the command priority at every router so higher-priority writes are forwarded before lower-priority application messages
Limit how many routers may forward the message
questions.explanation: Routers decrement Hop Count, preventing a routed message from circulating indefinitely.

questions.prompt: What does BACnet device address binding associate?
options: A Device instance with its BACnet network and MAC address
A user account with its password, certificate chain, application permissions, and preferred BACnet command priority
A trend record with its schedule, notification class, event-enrollment algorithm, acknowledgement state, and archival destination
A vendor ID with a UDP port
questions.explanation: Address binding lets a client translate a logical Device instance into the network-layer address needed to communicate.

questions.prompt: What is the key distinction between a generic IP default gateway and a BACnet router?
options: An IP default gateway maintains every BACnet Priority_Array and resolves competing commands before forwarding ordinary IP packets
The IP gateway routes IP packets; the BACnet router understands and routes BACnet NPDUs between BACnet networks
They are always identical functions because every device that forwards IP packets is required to parse and route BACnet NPDUs
A BACnet router only changes analog values
questions.explanation: A device may combine both roles, but IP routing and BACnet network-layer routing solve different addressing problems.

questions.prompt: Which physical layer is traditionally used by BACnet MS/TP?
options: Single-ended RS-232 multidrop
Analog 4-20 mA
EIA-485 balanced serial signaling
HDMI
questions.explanation: MS/TP uses EIA-485, commonly called RS-485, as its balanced multidrop physical layer.

questions.prompt: How do MS/TP manager nodes coordinate access to the bus?
options: They transmit whenever they want with no arbitration
A cloud server schedules every frame
They use IP multicast
They pass a token in a logical ring
questions.explanation: Token passing gives manager nodes deterministic opportunities to transmit on the shared EIA-485 bus.

questions.prompt: Which MAC address range can participate as MS/TP manager nodes?
options: 0 through 127
128 through 254 only
1 through 65535
255 only
questions.explanation: MS/TP manager nodes use addresses 0-127. Subordinate nodes may use 0-254, while 255 is the broadcast destination.

questions.prompt: What is MS/TP MAC address 255 used for?
options: A token timeout value that determines how long a manager waits before regenerating a lost token and restarting station discovery
Broadcast destination, not an assignable station address
The required address of the BACnet router that owns the token and coordinates all manager and subordinate transmissions on the segment
The mandatory address of the first manager node at the physical beginning of every correctly terminated EIA-485 trunk
questions.explanation: 255 denotes broadcast when used as a destination and is not valid as a station's own address.

questions.prompt: What does Max_Master control on an MS/TP network?
options: The number of BBMD peers, foreign-device registrations, and routed IP subnets that an MS/TP manager is permitted to advertise
The nominal EIA-485 differential voltage, bias current, termination resistance, cable impedance, and maximum permitted trunk length
The highest address considered when manager nodes search for peers
The maximum Device instance permitted on the internetwork and the highest BACnet network number that a router may advertise
questions.explanation: Max_Master bounds manager-node discovery. Setting it below an active manager's MAC can keep that node out of the token ring.

questions.prompt: What does Max_Info_Frames control?
options: The maximum number of objects a Device may expose across its Object_List before the controller must create another Device object
How many IP subnets, BBMD peers, foreign-device registrations, and BACnet network routes a manager may maintain
The largest trend buffer
How many information frames a manager may send when it holds the token
questions.explanation: Max_Info_Frames allocates how much traffic a manager can send per token possession and affects latency and bandwidth fairness.

questions.prompt: What happens if devices on one MS/TP segment use different baud rates?
options: They will not reliably decode one another's frames
They automatically negotiate using Who-Is
Only broadcasts are affected
A BBMD corrects the mismatch
questions.explanation: The shared serial segment must operate at a compatible baud rate; mismatches appear as silence, CRC errors, or corrupted traffic.

questions.prompt: What is a likely result of two MS/TP devices sharing the same MAC address?
options: A standards-defined redundant controller pair in which both stations intentionally share a MAC address for automatic failover
Token disruption and intermittent or conflicting responses
Faster communication because both devices can transmit during the same token hold while recipients combine their duplicate responses
Automatic address translation in which the router assigns each conflicting station a temporary MAC address and updates Device bindings
questions.explanation: Duplicate local MAC addresses make token ownership and replies ambiguous, commonly causing unstable communication.

questions.prompt: Which wiring topology is generally preferred for an EIA-485 MS/TP trunk?
options: A separate home run for every device tied together at one end
A closed electrical ring
A continuous daisy chain with short stubs
A large uncontrolled star
questions.explanation: A linear bus minimizes impedance discontinuities and reflections; long stubs and star branches degrade signal integrity.

questions.prompt: Where are termination resistors normally placed on an MS/TP segment?
options: At every device
Only at the middle device
Nowhere on any EIA-485 network
At the two physical ends of the main trunk
questions.explanation: Proper end-of-line termination at both physical ends matches the cable and reduces signal reflections.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of EIA-485 biasing on an MS/TP trunk?
options: Hold the idle bus in a known state when no driver is active
Increase the permitted Device instance range so stations with large instance numbers can participate on the same serial segment
Forward all local, remote, and global BACnet/IP broadcasts between configured IPv4 subnets without requiring BBMDs
Encrypt serial frames
questions.explanation: Bias resistors establish a defined idle differential state. Biasing must follow the transceiver and system design rather than being enabled indiscriminately everywhere.

questions.prompt: Why must the data-pair polarity be consistent along an MS/TP trunk?
options: Reversing the pair changes every Device object name and causes clients to rebuild their complete address-binding caches
Reversed polarity can prevent receivers from decoding the differential signal
Polarity assigns BACnet network numbers, Device instances, MS/TP MAC addresses, and command priorities according to conductor color
Polarity selects command priority
questions.explanation: EIA-485 receivers depend on consistent differential-pair polarity; one reversed device or segment can fail or disrupt communication.

questions.prompt: Which MS/TP node type must a BACnet router port be able to act as?
options: A BBMD foreign device that registers periodically with another BBMD and receives distributed BACnet/IP broadcasts over UDP
An analog input
A manager node that participates in token passing
A subordinate-only node
questions.explanation: A router must be able to initiate communications on the MS/TP network, which requires manager-node behavior.

questions.prompt: What is a practical advantage of assigning compact, consecutive MS/TP manager MAC addresses and tuning Max_Master?
options: It removes the need for end-of-line termination, biasing, shield continuity, and consistent EIA-485 data-pair polarity
It permits duplicate Device instances and duplicate MAC addresses because token polling automatically disambiguates the responding station
It converts MS/TP to BACnet/SC
Less time polling unused addresses and faster token maintenance
questions.explanation: Reducing gaps and setting Max_Master appropriately cuts Poll For Master overhead while preserving planned expansion room.

questions.prompt: Which BAS network uses the BACnet ARCNET data link at 156 kbps, commonly carried over an EIA-485 physical layer?
options: ARC156
MS/TP configured for 156 kbps over an Ethernet physical layer
BACnet/IPv4 using UDP port 156 on an EIA-485 trunk
BACnet/SC with its WebSocket frames converted directly to EIA-485 signaling
questions.explanation: ARC156 is the common Automated Logic BAS implementation of the BACnet ARCNET data link at 156 kbps over an EIA-485 physical layer. It remains distinct from BACnet MS/TP even though both can use EIA-485 wiring.

questions.prompt: What transport foundation does BACnet Secure Connect use?
options: SMTP email
TLS-secured WebSocket connections
Unencrypted UDP broadcast only
Serial token passing only
questions.explanation: BACnet/SC carries BVLC messages over secure WebSocket connections protected by TLS.

questions.prompt: What logical topology does a typical BACnet/SC network use?
options: A peer-to-peer UDP broadcast mesh in which every node must maintain a direct unencrypted connection to every other node
A Modbus register tree
Hub-and-spoke, with nodes connecting to a hub function
An electrical EIA-485 daisy chain
questions.explanation: Every BACnet/SC node supports a hub connection, creating the standard hub-and-spoke connectivity model.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a BACnet/SC failover hub?
options: Replace every BACnet router, BBMD, and application gateway in the internetwork whenever the primary hub is unavailable
Assign MS/TP MAC addresses
Store trend records
Provide an alternate hub connection if the primary hub is unavailable
questions.explanation: Nodes can connect to a configured failover hub when they cannot use the primary hub, improving availability.

questions.prompt: May BACnet/SC nodes establish direct connections for unicast traffic?
options: Yes, direct connections are optional and can bypass the hub for unicast
No; every unicast frame must traverse two BBMDs and both primary and failover hubs before reaching the destination node
Only over a dedicated MS/TP cable after the SC hub converts the TLS WebSocket connection into token-passing EIA-485 frames
Only without TLS
questions.explanation: BACnet/SC optionally supports direct secure WebSocket connections between nodes for unicast efficiency.

questions.prompt: What is a central operational role of certificates in BACnet/SC?
options: Replace Device instances, BACnet network numbers, and local MAC addresses with certificate serial numbers at every protocol layer
Establish trusted TLS identities for network participation
Set analog engineering units
Choose MS/TP baud rate
questions.explanation: Certificate trust supports authenticated, confidential, integrity-protected TLS connections between BACnet/SC peers.

questions.prompt: Which URI scheme identifies a TLS-secured WebSocket endpoint used by BACnet/SC?
options: ftp
snmp
wss
ws
questions.explanation: BACnet/SC uses secure WebSockets, represented by the wss URI scheme.

questions.prompt: Does admitting a device to a certificate-trusted BACnet/SC network automatically authorize every protected application operation?
options: Yes; admission by a trusted certificate grants unrestricted read, write, reinitialize, and device-control authority throughout the internetwork
Yes, TLS removes all need for policy
No, because BACnet/SC has no identity at all
No, trusted transport participation and application authorization are separate concerns
questions.explanation: TLS trust controls secure connectivity. Fine-grained permission for protected operations requires appropriate authentication and authorization policy.

questions.prompt: Why can BACnet/SC be easier to accommodate through modern firewalls than broadcast-oriented BACnet/IP?
options: It uses managed, persistent secure connections instead of relying on routed IP broadcasts
It disables BACnet routing and sends no traffic through managed firewall connections after the initial certificate exchange completes
It sends no network traffic
It uses analog wiring
questions.explanation: Hub connections provide explicit endpoints and connection flows, reducing dependence on broadcast forwarding and broadly opened UDP paths.

questions.prompt: What happens to the BACnet object and service model when BACnet/SC is used?
options: Only Device objects remain; every other standard object and service is replaced by WebSocket-specific resources and operations
It remains the BACnet application model; BACnet/SC changes the secure data-link transport
It is replaced by Modbus objects
All objects become proprietary
questions.explanation: BACnet/SC is a BACnet data-link option. Standard objects, services, and network-layer concepts continue above it.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly compares BACnet/SC with placing BACnet/IP inside a generic VPN?
options: A generic VPN rewrites every BACnet Device instance, network number, object identifier, and command priority as packets cross the tunnel
BACnet/SC cannot use IP infrastructure
BACnet/SC is standardized within BACnet and defines BACnet-aware secure connectivity; a VPN is a separate network overlay
They are identical protocols
questions.explanation: Both may protect traffic, but BACnet/SC defines secure BACnet virtual-link behavior, hubs, peers, and BACnet-specific connection management.

questions.prompt: What does an object's Event_State property indicate?
options: Its complete IPv4 configuration, including subnet mask, default gateway, DNS servers, UDP port, and current BBMD registration lifetime
Its MS/TP baud rate
Its vendor ID
Its current event condition such as normal, fault, offnormal, high limit, or low limit
questions.explanation: Event_State reports the object's current event state using a standardized enumeration appropriate to its event algorithm.

questions.prompt: What does Ack_Required indicate in BACnet event reporting?
options: Whether a transition requires acknowledgement according to the event configuration
Whether every ReadProperty request requires a password, certificate challenge, operator acknowledgement, and a confirmed event response
Whether the device supports IP
Whether a trend buffer is full
questions.explanation: Acknowledgement requirements are configured per event transition, commonly to-offnormal, to-fault, and to-normal.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a Notification Class object?
options: Configure EIA-485 bias, end-of-line termination, data-pair polarity, trunk length, baud rate, and repeater placement for serial networks
Define event priorities, acknowledgement requirements, and recipient routing
Store analog Present_Value history
Route NPDUs between networks
questions.explanation: Notification Class centralizes how event transitions are prioritized and delivered to configured recipients.

questions.prompt: What is an Event Enrollment object used for?
options: Enroll a station in an MS/TP token ring while assigning its MAC address, Max_Master value, baud rate, and token-retry timing
Create a TLS certificate
Apply an event algorithm to monitor a referenced value, often when event detection is not intrinsic to that object
Register a foreign BACnet/IP device
questions.explanation: Event Enrollment supports algorithmic event detection by referencing monitored properties and event parameters.

questions.prompt: What normally appears in each Trend Log record?
options: A BDT peer only
A TLS private key
The entire controller program, object database, certificate store, routing table, and current BBMD configuration at the sample time
A timestamp plus a logged value or status/error indication
questions.explanation: Trend records pair time with the sampled or triggered datum and associated status information.

questions.prompt: What does a Trend Log's Stop_When_Full setting control?
options: Whether logging stops at capacity instead of overwriting the oldest records
Whether all COV subscriptions expire immediately whenever the trend buffer reaches its configured record capacity
Whether the Device reboots
Whether BBMD forwarding stops
questions.explanation: When Stop_When_Full is false, a full circular log can overwrite oldest records; when true, collection stops at capacity.

questions.prompt: Why is reliable time synchronization important in a BACnet system?
options: It automatically corrects reversed EIA-485 polarity and recalculates termination resistance based on the current device count
It makes alarms, trends, schedules, and audit sequences comparable across devices
It assigns network numbers
It eliminates all broadcasts
questions.explanation: Unsynchronized clocks make event ordering, logs, schedule execution, and diagnosis unreliable.

questions.prompt: A schedule consistently executes one hour early after a seasonal clock change. What should be checked first?
options: Only the BBMD Broadcast Distribution Table, because seasonal time changes are calculated exclusively by broadcast-distribution peers
The object Vendor_Identifier
Device time, UTC offset, daylight-saving configuration, and time-sync source
MS/TP termination resistance only
questions.explanation: A consistent one-hour shift points to local time, offset, DST, or synchronization configuration rather than the schedule values themselves.

questions.prompt: What does a Calendar object represent?
options: A complete inventory of IP routers, their reachable BACnet networks, hop counts, BBMD peers, and foreign-device registrations
A command priority array
A table of vendor IDs
A reusable set of dates or date ranges for exception logic
questions.explanation: Calendar objects let schedules and other logic reference date lists, ranges, and recurring date patterns.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between intrinsic and algorithmic event detection?
options: Intrinsic detection is built into the monitored object; algorithmic detection is represented separately, commonly with Event Enrollment
Intrinsic events are available only on BACnet/IP objects, while algorithmic events are available only on MS/TP and ARC156 devices regardless of object type
Only algorithmic events have timestamps
There is no difference
questions.explanation: Some object types contain their own event parameters, while Event Enrollment can apply a separate standard event algorithm to referenced data.

questions.prompt: What is a BACnet PICS?
options: A mandatory cloud subscription that stores live object values, trend records, alarm recipients, and controller credentials for a BACnet product
A Protocol Implementation Conformance Statement listing a product's BACnet capabilities
A packet-capture image
A wiring termination standard
questions.explanation: The PICS describes supported BIBBs, object types, data links, character sets, segmentation, and other implementation capabilities.

questions.prompt: What does a BACnet Interoperability Building Block describe?
options: An IPv4 subnet
A required TLS cipher suite, certificate format, private-key storage mechanism, and firewall policy used by every BACnet data link
A defined interoperable capability composed of one or more services and related requirements
A physical enclosure for a controller
questions.explanation: BIBBs group service roles and related requirements into capabilities that can be specified and compared.

questions.prompt: What does BTL certification primarily indicate?
options: The product is guaranteed to satisfy every possible sequence of operation, control-loop requirement, and site-specific acceptance test
The product requires no commissioning
The product is made by ASHRAE
The product was independently tested against applicable BACnet conformance and interoperability requirements
questions.explanation: BTL certification provides evidence of tested BACnet implementation; project-specific application behavior still requires design and commissioning.

questions.prompt: What is ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135.1 used for?
options: Methods of test for BACnet conformance
Electrical installation code for all buildings
IP address allocation
Writing controller sequences
questions.explanation: Standard 135 defines BACnet, while Standard 135.1 defines procedures for testing claimed BACnet capabilities.

questions.prompt: What does a BACnet Vendor Identifier identify?
options: An alarm recipient
The organization assigned that vendor number
A unique device on the internetwork
A BACnet network segment
questions.explanation: Vendor IDs identify organizations and provide a namespace for proprietary extensions; they do not replace unique Device instances.

questions.prompt: What does a device's Protocol_Revision communicate?
options: Its IP subnet prefix
The expiration date of its BTL certificate together with the laboratory, test suite, and technician that approved the listing
The BACnet protocol revision implemented by the device
Its firmware build date only
questions.explanation: Protocol_Revision helps clients understand which standardized revision and associated features the device implements.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a BACnet device profile?
options: Assign a unique IP address
Replace the PICS entirely
Define the building mechanical schedule, occupied modes, alarm routing, trend intervals, and every sequence of operation for a project
Define a recognized set of minimum BACnet capabilities for a device role
questions.explanation: Profiles establish role-oriented capability baselines, but the PICS is still needed to understand a product's complete implementation.

questions.prompt: Does a BTL listing guarantee that two products implement the owner's sequence of operation correctly?
options: No, it supports protocol conformance and interoperability but does not replace application design and functional testing
Yes; listing guarantees every owner sequence, controller program, mechanical response, alarm route, and site-specific functional test without commissioning
Yes, if both use UDP 47808
No, because BTL tests only electrical safety
questions.explanation: BTL testing reduces protocol-integration risk. Controls logic, naming, graphics, sequences, and project requirements still need verification.

questions.prompt: May a BACnet product implement proprietary object types or properties?
options: Only on MS/TP
Yes, within assigned vendor-specific ranges and with adequate documentation
No; the standard forbids all vendor extensions, private properties, proprietary object types, and product-specific capability documentation
Only if it abandons standard objects
questions.explanation: BACnet reserves vendor-specific namespaces so innovation can coexist with standard interoperable capabilities; clients may need vendor documentation.

questions.prompt: What is the best starting point when specifying required BACnet interoperability?
options: Choose a UDP port and omit all application requirements
Assume every product labeled BACnet supports every standard service, object type, data link, device profile, and optional interoperability feature
State required functional capabilities, applicable BIBBs/profiles, data links, objects, and project acceptance tests
Require only that the word BACnet appear on the datasheet
questions.explanation: A testable capability specification and commissioning plan are more reliable than a generic BACnet requirement.

questions.prompt: A workstation discovers a device by I-Am but every ReadProperty request times out. What is a strong first hypothesis?
options: The device has no Device object
Who-Is and I-Am automatically prove every forward and return unicast path, firewall rule, router binding, and advertised address is usable
The trend buffer is full
Discovery reached the workstation, but the advertised return address, routing, firewall, or unicast path is unusable
questions.explanation: Broadcast discovery and subsequent unicast communication can follow different paths. Validate the source address, address binding, routes, NAT, and firewall policy.

questions.prompt: Two controllers use the same Device instance. What symptom is most likely?
options: Ambiguous discovery and address binding, with communication switching between devices
Standards-defined controller clustering with automatic failover, synchronized Priority_Arrays, and no effect on discovery or address binding
Automatic device clustering
Only a cosmetic name conflict
questions.explanation: Duplicate Device instances break the assumption that one logical identifier maps to one BACnet device.

questions.prompt: A remote laptop registered as a foreign device stops receiving broadcasts after several minutes. What should be checked?
options: Only MS/TP Max_Info_Frames, token-retry timing, serial termination, and manager MAC addressing on the nearest unrelated EIA-485 trunk
Registration renewal, time-to-live, BBMD FDT state, and return-path reachability
Analog input Units
Schedule exception dates only
questions.explanation: Foreign registration expires unless renewed, and NAT/firewall changes can also invalidate the BBMD's path to the registered address.

questions.prompt: A commandable output ignores a new write even though the service succeeds. What should be inspected first?
options: The Device Vendor_Identifier
The termination, bias voltage, baud rate, polarity, and Max_Master configuration of an unrelated MS/TP trunk elsewhere in the building
Priority_Array for a higher-priority active command and the priority used by the new write
The BBMD BDT
questions.explanation: A successful lower-priority write can be masked by a higher-priority value. Inspect the full Priority_Array and Relinquish_Default.

questions.prompt: A BACnet internetwork experiences a broadcast storm immediately after a BBMD configuration change. What is the best first review?
options: Increase every trend buffer
Change all Device instances
Disable every confirmed service, COV subscription, trend log, event notification, and router advertisement across the complete BACnet internetwork
Check BDT topology for duplicate, reciprocal-loop, mask, or addressing errors and inspect captured BVLL forwarding
questions.explanation: A malformed broadcast-distribution topology can replicate traffic. Review peer entries and packet traces before making unrelated application changes.

questions.prompt: An EIA-485 receiver measures +2.35 V at its non-inverting input and +2.05 V at its inverting input. What is guaranteed?
options: A high state, because the differential input is +300 mV
An undefined state, because the differential is below 1.5 V
A low state, because both input voltages are positive
An invalid state, because common mode must equal zero volts
questions.explanation: The receiver evaluates the difference between its inputs: 2.35 V − 2.05 V = +0.30 V. That exceeds the +200 mV threshold, while the +2.20 V common-mode level remains inside the allowed range.

references.title: Analog Devices AN-960: RS-485/RS-422 Circuit Implementation Guide
references.locator: Receiver differential sensitivity and common-mode range

questions.prompt: Before BACnet addressing, topology, and product limits are applied, what theoretical receiver count corresponds to 1/4-unit-load EIA-485 transceivers?
options: 64 receivers before accounting for other limits
128 receivers before accounting for other limits
256 receivers under the same electrical calculation
32 receivers because fractional loads do not add
questions.explanation: Each quarter-unit-load receiver consumes 0.25 UL; 32 divided by 0.25 equals 128 theoretical receivers.

questions.prompt: A loaded-driver compliance test measures 1.2 V differential across the EIA-485 test load. How should that result be interpreted?
options: It passes because any differential above 200 mV satisfies the driver test
It passes because the loaded-driver minimum is exactly 1.0 V differential
It fails the 1.5 V loaded-driver minimum, even though a receiver may switch
It fails only if the common-mode voltage is also outside the permitted range
questions.explanation: Driver compliance and receiver sensitivity are different limits. A receiver threshold is ±200 mV, but the standard loaded-driver test requires at least 1.5 V differential output, so 1.2 V fails.

references.title: TI RS-485 Basics Series
references.locator: Driver output test and receiver threshold comparison

questions.prompt: Which minimum receiver input resistance represents one standard EIA-485 unit load at the 12 V test point?
options: 96 kΩ, equivalent to one-eighth unit load
48 kΩ, equivalent to one-quarter unit load
24 kΩ, equivalent to one-half unit load
12 kΩ, equivalent to one full unit load
questions.explanation: One unit load is represented by 1 mA at 12 V, equivalent to a 12 kΩ minimum input resistance. Fractional-load receivers have proportionally higher input resistance.

questions.prompt: A mixed EIA-485 segment has 20 full-unit-load receivers and 24 half-unit-load receivers. What is its receiver loading?
options: 32 UL, exactly the nominal segment load budget
44 UL, because each package counts as one load
22 UL, after averaging the two receiver groups
64 UL, the limit for all fractional-load devices
questions.explanation: The total is 20 × 1 UL plus 24 × 0.5 UL, or 32 UL. Device count alone is not the electrical loading calculation.

questions.prompt: For a conventional EIA-485 receiver, which differential input guarantees the non-inverting input is recognized as high?
options: At least +50 mV across the receiver inputs
At least +200 mV across the receiver inputs
At least +1.5 V measured to signal ground
At least +5 V measured between both inputs
questions.explanation: A conventional EIA-485 receiver guarantees one state at +200 mV or greater differential input and the opposite state at −200 mV or less.

references.title: Analog Devices AN-960: RS-485/RS-422 Circuit Implementation Guide

questions.prompt: What does the base EIA-485 threshold specification guarantee when the differential input is between −200 mV and +200 mV?
options: A guaranteed logic zero throughout that interval
A guaranteed logic one throughout that interval
No defined conventional-receiver output in that interval
A guaranteed alternating output at the baud rate
questions.explanation: The conventional receiver output is undefined inside the ±200 mV threshold band. True fail-safe receivers add behavior beyond that basic guarantee.

references.title: Analog Devices AN-1458: Isolated RS-485 with Integrated Transformer Driver
references.locator: Standard receiver threshold and true fail-safe discussion

questions.prompt: Which common-mode input range must a standard EIA-485 receiver tolerate while detecting the differential signal?
options: 0 V through +5 V only at both conductors
−12 V through +12 V relative to shield
−5 V through +5 V relative to local common
−7 V through +12 V at the receiver inputs
questions.explanation: EIA-485 receivers are specified to operate with input common-mode voltage from −7 V to +12 V while evaluating the differential voltage.

references.title: Analog Devices AN-960: RS-485/RS-422 Circuit Implementation Guide

questions.prompt: Across the standard loaded EIA-485 driver test circuit, what differential output range is expected?
options: At least 1.5 V and no more than 5 V
At least 0.2 V and no more than 1 V
At least 5 V and no more than 12 V
Exactly 2.5 V with zero permitted tolerance
questions.explanation: The loaded driver test requires at least 1.5 V differential output and limits it to 5 V; the receiver threshold is much lower at ±200 mV.

references.title: TI RS-485 Basics Series
references.locator: Driver output test, 1.5 V < VOD < 5 V

questions.prompt: Why is approximately 54 Ω used in the EIA-485 loaded-driver compliance test?
options: It models one 54 Ω cable with no termination or receivers
It represents the worst-case parallel effect of terminations and receiver loads
It forces each receiver input to consume exactly two unit loads
It is the required characteristic impedance for BACnet MS/TP cable
questions.explanation: The compliance load approximates the heavy parallel loading produced by two end terminations together with the allowed receiver unit loads; it is not the cable impedance.

references.title: TI RS-485 Basics Series
references.locator: Figure 4 and 54 Ω loaded-driver test discussion

questions.prompt: Before receiver loading is included, what DC load do two 120 Ω end-of-line terminators present to the driver?
options: 240 Ω because the two terminators are in series
120 Ω because only the far terminator is visible
60 Ω because both terminators are in parallel
54 Ω because cable impedance changes each resistor
questions.explanation: From the differential driver's perspective, the two 120 Ω end terminations are parallel, producing 60 Ω before receiver input loading is added.

questions.prompt: What electrical state should an EIA-485 transceiver enter when its driver-enable input is deasserted?
options: Drive both conductors high through low impedance
Drive a continuous alternating synchronization pattern
Short the pair together to suppress reflections
Present a high-impedance, tri-stated driver output
questions.explanation: Deasserting driver enable places the driver outputs in a high-impedance state so another station can drive the shared bus.

references.title: Analog Devices AN-960: RS-485/RS-422 Circuit Implementation Guide

questions.prompt: On a two-wire half-duplex MS/TP segment, how many stations may actively drive the pair at one instant during normal operation?
options: One station; all other drivers must be high impedance
Two stations, provided their transmitted bits agree
Every manager currently represented in the token ring
All stations while the token frame is being repeated
questions.explanation: Two-wire EIA-485 is a shared half-duplex medium. Only the current transmitter may enable its driver; simultaneous drivers create contention.

references.title: Analog Devices AN-960: RS-485/RS-422 Circuit Implementation Guide

questions.prompt: A receiver sees +14 V on one input and +12 V on the other. The 2 V differential is adequate; what remains wrong?
options: The differential is below the 200 mV receiver threshold
The +13 V common-mode level exceeds the +12 V limit
The pair has exactly the required 2 V common-mode level
Nothing; differential amplitude is the only EIA-485 limit
questions.explanation: The average input level is +13 V, outside the standard +12 V common-mode ceiling, even though the 2 V differential amplitude is healthy.

references.title: Analog Devices AN-960: RS-485/RS-422 Circuit Implementation Guide
references.locator: Differential sensitivity and −7 V to +12 V common-mode range

questions.prompt: After how much qualifying silence does an MS/TP manager conclude that the token has been lost?
options: 20 ms of silence after the previous octet
255 ms of silence after a confirmed request
500 ms without a data-available or receive-error event
1,000 ms without receiving a complete token frame
questions.explanation: Tno_token is 500 ms without a DataAvailable or ReceiveError event. The node then enters the no-token recovery process.

questions.prompt: What is the width of each address-based token-generation slot during MS/TP lost-token recovery?
options: 1 ms per station-address slot
5 ms per station-address slot
20 milliseconds per station-address time slot
10 ms per station-address slot
questions.explanation: Tslot is 10 ms. A manager's address offsets its token-generation window after Tno_token.

questions.prompt: Which expression gives the start of a fixed-address manager's token-generation window after token loss?
options: Tno_token + (Tslot × this station address)
Treply_timeout + (Tslot × next station address)
Tusage_delay × Max_Info_Frames × station address
Tframe_abort + Tturnaround + one token rotation
questions.explanation: The NO_TOKEN state assigns each manager a window beginning at Tno_token + Tslot × TS, where TS is its station address. Lower addresses therefore get earlier recovery opportunities.

questions.prompt: With Tno_token = 500 ms and Tslot = 10 ms, when does station address 37 first enter its token-generation window?
options: At 537 ms after qualifying silence begins
At 870 ms after qualifying silence begins
At 3,700 ms after qualifying silence begins
At 5,000 ms after qualifying silence begins
questions.explanation: The start is 500 ms + (10 ms × 37) = 870 ms. A lower-address manager would receive an earlier slot.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum Tusage_delay after receiving a Token or Poll For Master before beginning a frame?
options: 5 ms after the previous frame ends
10 ms after the previous frame ends
15 ms after the previous frame ends
20 ms after the prior token or poll frame ends
questions.explanation: Tusage_delay is 15 ms: the maximum wait after receiving a token or Poll For Master before transmitting the first octet.

questions.prompt: Which range correctly describes Tusage_timeout for waiting on token use or a Poll For Master reply?
options: At least 5 ms and never more than 10 ms
At least 10 ms and never more than 15 ms
At least 15 ms and never more than 40 ms in service
At least 20 ms and never more than 35 ms
questions.explanation: The minimum Tusage_timeout is 20 ms; an implementation may use a larger value, but not more than 35 ms.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum Treply_delay for starting either a reply or Reply Postponed after a request frame?
options: 250 ms from reception of the request frame
255 ms from transmission of the request frame
300 ms from reception of the token frame
500 ms from the last observed bus activity
questions.explanation: A responding node has at most 250 ms to begin a reply or send Reply Postponed after receiving a frame that expects a reply.

questions.prompt: Which limits apply to Treply_timeout while waiting for a station to begin replying to a confirmed request?
options: Minimum 200 ms, with no specified upper bound
Minimum 255 ms, and an implementation may not exceed 300 ms
Exactly 250 ms, with no implementation tolerance
Minimum 500 ms, plus one slot per destination address
questions.explanation: Treply_timeout is at least 255 ms. Implementations may wait longer, but the value may not exceed 300 ms.

questions.prompt: What minimum turnaround interval follows the final stop bit of a received frame before enabling a transmitter?
options: 10 bit times after the final received stop bit
20 bit times after the final received stop bit
40 bit times after the final received stop bit
60 bit times after the final received stop bit elapses
questions.explanation: Tturnaround is 40 bit times. Because it is expressed in bit times, its wall-clock duration changes with baud rate.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Tframe_abort while a receiver is waiting for the next octet of a frame?
options: It is fixed at 20 bit times for every implementation
It is fixed at 40 bit times for every implementation
It starts at 500 ms and has no upper time limit
It is at least 60 bit times and may not exceed 100 ms
questions.explanation: A receiver may discard an interrupted frame after at least 60 bit times of silence; implementations may use a larger timeout, capped at 100 ms.

questions.prompt: What is the maximum idle interval a transmitting MS/TP node may allow between octets within one frame?
options: 20 bit times, defined by Tframe_gap
40 bit times, defined by Tturnaround
60 bit times, defined by Tframe_abort
500 ms, defined by Tno_token
questions.explanation: Tframe_gap limits a sender to no more than 20 bit times of idle line between octets of the same frame.

questions.prompt: After how many token uses does the Npoll counter trigger periodic Poll For Master maintenance?
options: 25 token uses before the maintenance poll
50 token uses before the maintenance poll
100 token uses before the maintenance poll
127 token uses before the maintenance poll
questions.explanation: Npoll is 50. Periodic polling lets a manager discover stations that have joined between it and its known successor.

questions.prompt: How many token retransmission retries does Nretry_token permit before the sender searches for a new successor?
options: Zero retries after the first token transmission
Two retries after the first token transmission
One retry after the first token transmission
Three retries after the first token transmission
questions.explanation: Nretry_token is 1. After the permitted retry fails to provoke successor activity, the manager begins searching for a new successor.

questions.prompt: What does increasing one manager's Max_Info_Frames primarily change on an MS/TP network?
options: It increases the maximum legal differential bus voltage
It raises the manager's permitted station address range
It shortens the receiver's EIA-485 common-mode range
It lets that manager send more information frames per token hold
questions.explanation: Max_Info_Frames controls how many information frames that manager may transmit before passing the token, so it can allocate more link bandwidth while increasing token-hold time.

questions.prompt: Why can setting Max_Master to the highest manager address actually in use improve a compact MS/TP trunk?
options: It avoids polling unused higher addresses and returns bandwidth to normal traffic
It increases every transceiver's receiver input resistance above one unit load
It permits subordinate addresses above 254 without adding another network
It eliminates token passing and converts the segment to collision detection
questions.explanation: A correctly reduced Max_Master bounds the Poll For Master search so the ring spends less time probing unused addresses. It must still include the highest manager address present.

references.title: NISTIR 6392 BACnet specification guidance
references.locator: Section 6.3.3, MS/TP MAC addresses and Max_Master

questions.prompt: When a station cannot produce a requested response within Treply_delay, what does an MS/TP Reply Postponed frame accomplish?
options: It permanently cancels the request and deletes its transaction state
It satisfies the immediate data-link timing while indicating the response will come later
It transfers the token directly to the original requester for an unlimited interval
It changes the request into an unconfirmed broadcast for every station
questions.explanation: Reply Postponed prevents the requester from treating the absence of an immediate response as a link-layer timeout while the actual response is deferred.

questions.prompt: How does ARC156 limit a controller's transmission opportunity each time its ARCNET coprocessor receives the token?
options: It may send one data packet, then it must pass the token
It may retain the token for a configurable Max_Info_Frames count
It may send until a 250 ms token-hold timer expires
It may send every queued packet before passing the token
questions.explanation: ARC156 permits one data packet per token possession and does not let a controller keep the token. This differs fundamentally from MS/TP Max_Info_Frames behavior.

references.title: Automated Logic ARC156 Wiring Technical Instructions

questions.prompt: Why do active ARC156 controllers not need sequential MAC addresses for efficient token passing?
options: Every unused numerical address receives and immediately rejects a separately transmitted token
The logical token loop includes only controllers that exist on the network
A BBMD translates sparse MAC addresses into a consecutive sequence
ARC156 broadcasts every token so no successor relationship exists
questions.explanation: The ARCNET coprocessors maintain a logical loop of participating controllers, so the token passes only to controllers that exist rather than polling each numerical gap.

references.title: Automated Logic ARC156 Wiring Technical Instructions

questions.prompt: What happens when an ARC156 controller fails to respond when the logical token loop addresses it?
options: It remains in the logical loop and receives unlimited repeated token transmissions
It becomes the permanent token regeneration controller
It drops from the loop until a network reconfiguration admits it again
It forces every controller to change to MS/TP timing immediately
questions.explanation: A controller that does not respond to its token is removed from the active loop and does not receive another token until network reconfiguration.

references.title: Automated Logic ARC156 Wiring Technical Instructions

questions.prompt: Approximately how long does the ARC156 network reconfiguration process take when rebuilding its participating token loop?
options: About 13 milliseconds under all network loads
About 50 milliseconds for each unused MAC address
About 500 milliseconds, identical to MS/TP Tno_token
About 3 seconds for the network reconfiguration
questions.explanation: The ARC156 wiring guidance states that a network reconfiguration takes about three seconds.

references.title: Automated Logic ARC156 Wiring Technical Instructions

questions.prompt: When does an operating ARC156 controller initiate network reconfiguration because it has stopped seeing the token?
options: After about 13 seconds without receiving the token
After exactly 500 milliseconds without receiving any valid network octet
After 50 token rotations without Poll For Master
After one failed BACnet confirmed service request
questions.explanation: A newly powered controller, or one that has not received the token for about 13 seconds, initiates ARC156 network reconfiguration.

references.title: Automated Logic ARC156 Wiring Technical Instructions

questions.prompt: Which protocol pairing defines native BACnet/Ethernet in BACnet’s collapsed architecture?
options: BVLL over UDP and IPv4, followed by an Ethernet II payload
ISO 8802-2 Type 1 logical-link control over ISO 8802-3 Ethernet
MS/TP framing over an EIA-485 physical Ethernet segment
Secure Connect BVLL directly over IEEE 802.3 Ethernet without WebSockets or any TLS transport
questions.explanation: Native BACnet/Ethernet uses ISO 8802-2 Type 1 over ISO 8802-3. BACnet/IP is a separate datalink using BVLL, UDP, and IP.

references.title: ANSI/ASHRAE Addendum bj to Standard 135-2016
references.locator: Clause 4.1, Figure 4-2, Table 6-1, and network/router definitions

questions.prompt: What maximum NPDU length does BACnet specify for the native ISO 8802-3 Ethernet datalink?
options: 501 octets, matching the original ARCNET NPDU constraint
1500 octets, consuming the Ethernet data field without LLC overhead
1497 octets, with three octets reserved for LLC
1476 octets, reserving space for UDP, IPv4, and BVLL headers
questions.explanation: Table 6-1 specifies a 1497-octet maximum NPDU for native BACnet/Ethernet. The three-octet LLC header occupies the remainder of the conventional 1500-octet Ethernet data field.

references.title: ANSI/ASHRAE Addendum bj to Standard 135-2016
references.locator: Clause 4.1, Figure 4-2, Table 6-1, and network/router definitions

questions.prompt: Which destination MAC address carries a local BACnet broadcast on native BACnet/Ethernet?
options: 00:00:00:00:00:00, the unspecified Ethernet station address
01:00:5E:BA:C0:00, multicast derived from the BACnet UDP port
The IPv4 subnet broadcast translated to an Ethernet address by ARP
FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF, the all-stations broadcast address
questions.explanation: Native BACnet/Ethernet uses the six-octet Ethernet broadcast MAC address FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF. This local datalink broadcast does not require IP or a BBMD.

questions.prompt: Two native BACnet/Ethernet segments are joined by transparent Ethernet bridges and retain one BACnet network number. How does BACnet classify the result?
options: One BACnet network containing multiple bridged segments
Two BACnet networks because each Ethernet bridge creates a network boundary
One BACnet/IP network because bridges automatically insert BVLL and UDP headers
A BACnet internetwork requiring every bridge to advertise an independent DNET
questions.explanation: BACnet defines a network as one or more segments interconnected by bridges with the same network address. A BACnet router connects distinct BACnet networks.

references.title: ANSI/ASHRAE Addendum bj to Standard 135-2016
references.locator: Clause 4.1, Figure 4-2, Table 6-1, and network/router definitions

questions.prompt: Which capture signature identifies native BACnet/Ethernet rather than BACnet/IP carried over Ethernet?
options: Ethernet II with IPv4, UDP port BAC0, and a BVLC header before the NPDU
IEEE 802.3 length framing, then BACnet LLC and the NPDU
An IEEE 802.1Q tag followed directly by an MS/TP preamble and token frame
An ARP payload resolving a BACnet device instance directly to an Ethernet MAC
questions.explanation: Native BACnet/Ethernet carries the NPDU directly through IEEE 802.2 LLC over IEEE 802.3. BACnet/IP adds BVLL, UDP, and IP encapsulation.

references.title: ANSI/ASHRAE Addendum bj to Standard 135-2016
references.locator: Clause 4.1, Figure 4-2, Table 6-1, and network/router definitions

questions.prompt: In an IPv4 fragment header, what unit does the 13-bit Fragment Offset field use?
options: Individual bits measured from the beginning of the complete Ethernet preamble
Four-octet words measured from the IPv4 header
Eight-octet units measured within the original IP payload
Whole Ethernet frames measured from the first fragment
questions.explanation: IPv4 Fragment Offset is expressed in eight-octet units. Consequently, every fragment except the final fragment must end on an eight-octet payload boundary.

questions.prompt: What does an all-zero UDP checksum field mean in an IPv4 UDP datagram under RFC 768?
options: The computed checksum was zero and must remain encoded as zero
The UDP payload contains exactly zero data octets
The IPv4 header checksum also covers the UDP payload
The transmitter generated no UDP checksum for that datagram
questions.explanation: For IPv4 UDP, an all-zero transmitted checksum indicates that no UDP checksum was generated. A computed checksum result of zero is transmitted as all ones instead.

questions.prompt: Which fields are included in the IPv4 UDP checksum pseudo-header to help detect misdelivery?
options: Source IP, destination IP, zero, protocol number, and UDP length
Source MAC, destination MAC, VLAN ID, and Ethernet FCS
IPv4 TTL, header checksum, fragment offset, and DSCP
BACnet network number, hop count, invoke ID, and APDU length
questions.explanation: The UDP pseudo-header contains the IPv4 source and destination addresses, a zero octet, protocol number, and UDP length; it is checksummed with the UDP header and data.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest valid value of the UDP Length field?
options: Four octets for the source and destination ports only
Eight octets for the UDP header with no payload
Twenty octets because UDP inherits the IPv4 header length
Forty-six octets to satisfy Ethernet payload padding
questions.explanation: UDP Length includes the eight-octet UDP header plus its data, so a header-only UDP datagram has a Length value of eight.

questions.prompt: What must an IPv4 forwarding module do to the Time To Live field while processing a datagram?
options: Leave TTL unchanged unless the datagram is fragmented
Increase TTL by one to account for forwarding latency
Decrease TTL by at least one and destroy the datagram at zero
Replace TTL with the Ethernet switch hop count
questions.explanation: RFC 791 requires every processing module to reduce TTL by at least one; a datagram whose TTL reaches zero is destroyed, bounding routing loops.

questions.prompt: A router receives an IPv4 datagram larger than the outgoing MTU with Don't Fragment set. What is the standards-based outcome?
options: The router clears DF and fragments the datagram normally
The router converts the datagram into multiple UDP messages
The router pads the Ethernet frame to the next supported MTU
The router discards it and can report fragmentation needed by ICMP
questions.explanation: DF prohibits router fragmentation. When the next-hop MTU is too small, the datagram is discarded; ICMP Destination Unreachable, fragmentation needed, supports path-MTU handling.

questions.prompt: Which BVLC function code identifies an Original-Unicast-NPDU in classic BACnet/IPv4?
options: 0x0A, carrying a directed BACnet NPDU
0x0B, carrying a local BACnet broadcast
0x09, requesting BBMD broadcast distribution
0x04, forwarding an NPDU from a BBMD
questions.explanation: Classic BACnet/IP uses BVLC function 0x0A for Original-Unicast-NPDU. The BVLC header preserves the datalink delivery mode for the BACnet stack.

questions.prompt: Which BVLC function code identifies an Original-Broadcast-NPDU in classic BACnet/IPv4?
options: 0x0A, the directed Original-Unicast-NPDU function
0x0B, the local Original-Broadcast-NPDU function
0x08, the Delete-Foreign-Device-Table-Entry function
0x05, the Register-Foreign-Device function
questions.explanation: BVLC function 0x0B marks an Original-Broadcast-NPDU sent by a non-foreign B/IP device or router to the B/IP broadcast address.

questions.prompt: What one-octet BVLC Type value identifies classic BACnet/IPv4 BVLL messages?
options: 0x01, matching the BACnet NPDU protocol version
0x82, matching the BACnet LLC service access point
0x81, identifying the BVLL for BACnet/IPv4
0xBAC0, matching the default UDP port
questions.explanation: The classic BACnet/IP BVLC header begins with the one-octet type value 0x81. The default UDP port 0xBAC0 is a separate transport-layer value.

questions.prompt: What is the required default behavior for an IP router receiving an IPv4 directed broadcast under RFC 2644?
options: Forward every directed broadcast to preserve legacy discovery
Convert it to multicast before forwarding to the destination subnet
Forward it only when the UDP destination port is 47808
Disable directed-broadcast forwarding by default
questions.explanation: RFC 2644 changed router requirements so directed-broadcast forwarding is disabled by default, limiting amplification attacks. BACnet broadcast distribution therefore cannot assume ordinary routers forward it.

references.title: RFC 2644: Changing the Default for Directed Broadcasts in Routers

questions.prompt: Which EtherType identifies an IPv4 datagram carried directly in an Ethernet II frame?
options: 0x0800 for Internet Protocol version 4
0x8100 for an IEEE 802.1Q customer VLAN tag
0x86DD for Internet Protocol version 6
0x0806 for the Address Resolution Protocol
questions.explanation: RFC 894 specifies EtherType 0x0800 for IPv4 over Ethernet. The other values identify VLAN tagging, IPv6, and ARP respectively.

references.title: RFC 894: IP Datagrams over Ethernet Networks

questions.prompt: How is an IPv4 packet shorter than Ethernet's 46-octet minimum data field carried?
options: The IPv4 Total Length is increased to include arbitrary application data
The Ethernet data field is padded, but the padding is outside IP Total Length
The frame is transmitted below the minimum because IPv4 is exempt
The UDP checksum bytes are repeated until the frame reaches 46 octets
questions.explanation: Ethernet padding brings the data field to 46 octets, but that padding is not part of the IPv4 packet and is excluded from the IP Total Length field.

references.title: RFC 894: IP Datagrams over Ethernet Networks

questions.prompt: What standard Ethernet MTU limits an unfragmented IPv4 datagram carried using Ethernet II encapsulation?
options: 1,492 octets after reserving an eight-octet LLC/SNAP header
1,518 octets including Ethernet addresses and frame check sequence
1,500 octets of Ethernet payload available to the IPv4 datagram
1,522 octets because every IPv4 frame contains an 802.1Q tag
questions.explanation: The conventional Ethernet MTU exposed to IPv4 is 1,500 octets. Ethernet header, optional tag, and FCS accounting are outside that IP MTU.

references.title: RFC 894: IP Datagrams over Ethernet Networks
references.locator: Maximum IP datagram length; see verified errata 570

questions.prompt: How much does one IEEE 802.1Q customer VLAN tag add to the Ethernet MAC frame?
options: One octet inserted before the destination address
Two octets replacing the original EtherType field
Eight octets appended after the frame check sequence
Four octets inserted after the source MAC address
questions.explanation: An 802.1Q tag is 32 bits, or four octets, and is inserted after the source MAC address before the original type/length information.

questions.prompt: Which Tag Protocol Identifier normally marks an IEEE 802.1Q customer VLAN tag?
options: 0x8100 in the tag protocol identifier field
0x0800 in the tag control information field
0xBAC0 in the priority code point field
0xFFFF in the VLAN identifier field
questions.explanation: The customer VLAN tag TPID is 0x8100. It identifies the following tag control information rather than an IPv4 payload.

questions.prompt: How is the 16-bit 802.1Q Tag Control Information field divided?
options: Eight priority bits followed by eight VLAN bits
Three PCP bits, one DEI bit, and twelve VID bits
Four EtherType bits followed by twelve checksum bits
One broadcast bit, seven priority bits, and eight port bits
questions.explanation: The TCI contains a three-bit Priority Code Point, one Drop Eligible Indicator bit, and a twelve-bit VLAN Identifier.

questions.prompt: What maximum basic MAC frame sizes distinguish an untagged Ethernet frame from a singly tagged frame?
options: 1,500 untagged and 1,504 tagged, excluding every MAC header field
1,514 untagged and 1,518 tagged, excluding the frame check sequence
1,518 untagged and 1,522 tagged, including the frame check sequence
1,522 untagged and 1,526 tagged, including preamble and interpacket gap
questions.explanation: The standard basic MAC frame maximum is 1,518 octets untagged and 1,522 octets with one VLAN tag, counting the FCS but not preamble or interpacket gap.

questions.prompt: Which LLC service access point value is assigned to BACnet for both DSAP and SSAP?
options: 0x81, also used as the classic BACnet/IP BVLC type
0xCD, the BACnet ARCNET system code
0x03, the unnumbered-information LLC control value
0x82 for both the destination and source service access points
questions.explanation: BACnet's IEEE 802.2 logical-link service access point is 0x82 for both DSAP and SSAP. The control field is a separate LLC field.

references.title: BACnet Committee Encoding Examples
references.locator: BACnet LLC SSAP and DSAP values

questions.prompt: What does ARP resolve before IPv4 traffic can be sent to an on-link next hop over Ethernet?
options: The next-hop IPv4 address to its 48-bit Ethernet hardware address
The BACnet Device instance to its BACnet network number
The UDP destination port to an IEEE 802.1Q VLAN ID
The remote subnet mask to an Ethernet frame check sequence
questions.explanation: ARP maps the protocol address selected as the local next hop to the 48-bit Ethernet address needed for link-layer delivery.

references.title: RFC 826: An Ethernet Address Resolution Protocol

questions.prompt: How can a receiver distinguish an IEEE 802.3 Length field from an Ethernet II EtherType in the same header position?
options: Length values are above 0x8000 while EtherTypes are below 64
A value at or below 1500 is a length; valid EtherTypes are greater than 1500
The destination MAC multicast bit selects between length and type
Only the presence of an IPv4 checksum distinguishes the two formats
questions.explanation: The shared two-octet field is interpreted as an IEEE 802.3 length when it is 1500 or less; assigned EtherType values occupy the range above 1500.
